message.content: {"12385_8353800664317": {"answer": "C", "reason": "The combination of a persistent tubular opacity (mucocele) and surrounding hyperlucent lung (hyperinflation due to collateral ventilation) in the left upper lobe is the classic radiographic presentation of congenital bronchial atresia."}, "12385_8353800681551": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The specific finding of a tubular opacity representing an impacted mucus plug distal to an atretic segment, accompanied by adjacent hyperlucency from air trapping, is pathognomonic for congenital bronchial atresia."}, "12385_8353800688953": {"answer": "B", "reason": "The persistence of the tubular opacity and surrounding hyperlucent area indicates a static congenital anomaly rather than an infectious or neoplastic process, consistent with bronchial atresia featuring a mucocele and collateral hyperinflation."}, "12385_8353800689343": {"answer": "C", "reason": "Congenital bronchial atresia is a stable developmental anomaly; therefore, the radiographic findings of the tubular opacity and hyperlucent area typically remain unchanged over time, distinguishing it from progressive or resolving pathologies."}}
